page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton4 processor family, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration provides 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps. No GPUs are present.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and text processing. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance for cached small-block reads and strong performance for uncached large-block reads and writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier. However, single-core stress-ng performance and LLM inference speeds for 135M and 7B models fall into the average category.

From a resource density perspective, the c9g.16xlarge offers high compute density with 64 dedicated physical cores, making it efficient for parallelized workloads that benefit from a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core mapping. The lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The 2.0 GB per core memory allocation is optimized for compute-heavy tasks but may limit memory-bound applications.

This hardware profile is appropriate for highly parallelized compute-intensive workloads, including software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, database operations, and physics simulations. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference due to the average single-core performance and moderate memory-to-core ratio.
